Subject: Dedicated sizing ask — Chronos-XL (16k) and quant impact

Hi Grace,

Thanks for the demo last week. Novus is moving to a pilot that will serve clinical summarization inside our physician workflow; we expect bursts during morning rounds and nightly batch processing. A couple of details that will determine the reserved capacity we need:

- Model: Chronos-XL-16k (70B) — the team is testing both FP16 and an 8-bit quantized build.
- Typical request: ~120 tokens in prompt, ~800 tokens generation (most calls are long-form).
- Expected peak QPS: 20–30 (short bursts up to 40) during peak hours; average sustained QPS ~7–10.
- SLA expectations: p95 latency < 700ms when under batching; offline batches can be longer.

Can you give a ballpark for:
1) how many GPUs (and which SKUs) we should reserve for a Dedicated pool to cover the pilot (initial target concurrency ~30)
2) the delta if we use 8-bit quantization vs FP16 (memory and perf trade-offs)
3) any obvious risk areas (KV cache memory, long contexts, canary testing suggestions)

If helpful, Procurement copied here will start the paperwork once we have a sizing and a canary plan.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — Alicia

Hi Alicia — great to hear Novus is moving to pilot. I put together an initial sizing and a short playbook attached (novus-dedicated-sizing-v1.xlsx, chronos-xl-benchmarks-summary.pdf). High level summary below; see attachment for the assumptions and per-GPU throughput curves.

Quick summary (pilot: target concurrency 30, average ~8 QPS):
- FP16 baseline: Chronos-XL-16k tends to require a ~40–80GB working set depending on batch and KV cache strategy. For predictable latency and easier operational runbooks we recommend reserving 6 x NVIDIA A100-40GB-equivalent GPUs (or 3–4 x A100-80GB / H100-80GB) for the pilot. That gives headroom for canary traffic + rolling updates.
- 8-bit quantized: using our int8 path reduces model weights + activation memory by ~35–45% typically. For Novus this can drop the effective per-replica memory enough to run on 2–4 x A100-40GB replicas for the same nominal capacity, but expect a latency hit (~10–25%) and a small quality delta on long-form summarization.
- KV cache: long contexts (16k) increase the runtime working set linearly. If you want sub-700ms p95 we recommend keeping hot KV cache on-GPU; offloading KV to NVMe reduces GPU footprint but increases p95 significantly for tail latencies.

Operational recommendation: start the pilot with FP16 on 6 x A100-40GB-equivalent in a Dedicated pool, run a 2-week canary (traffic mirroring + small % live traffic) and a second canary with int8 quantized replicas to measure quality/latency in production traffic. If quant looks acceptable, we can convert a portion of serving capacity to int8 to save cost.

Next steps:
1) Confirm pilot dates and PO cadence — Procurement, can you share Novus’ preferred billing cadence?
2) We'll schedule a 60-min perf runbook session with Marcus and Marissa to review the attached numbers and agree on canary SLIs.
3) We’ll prepare a DocuSign-ready MPA for the pilot deposit (draft attached).

Happy to walk through the spreadsheet on a call later today.

— Grace

Looping in some extra detail for the canary plan and the memory math so we don't undercommit:

- Memory/footprint notes: the model weights for Chronos-XL-70B in FP16 are ~35–40GB resident. Runtime activations + kv-cache for 16k context add material overhead; in our internal runs we've seen KV/cache + activations push the working set to ~1.3–1.8x model weight when contexts average >8k, and closer to 2.0x at sustained 16k with batched inference. That matches why FP16 needs the larger SKUs.
- Quantization: our int8 pipeline reduces the model weights and many activations; practical memory savings are typically ~40% but results vary by model family and precision knobs. Important: int8 increases sensitivity of attention layers for long generations — run quality checks on your clinical prompts.
- GPU sku recommendation: for initial pilot we recommend A100-40GB in a 6-GPU pool (balanced across two AZs). If Novus requires tighter p95s, provision at least two H100-80/ A100-80 equivalents so we can keep headroom for bursts and background batch jobs.
- Autoscale/burst: include a small burst pool (2-3 cheaper GPUs) for nightly batch jobs to avoid impacting live latency.

Canary SLIs we should capture: p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, per-request tail (95–99.9), quality regression on held-out prompt set (we can use Novus clinical prompt set), and memory paging rates (if any).

I'll drop a short runbook with the commands to collect KV cache sizing and perf logs into the shared drive after this.

— Marcus
